# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[cd8839627f613225] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/response; selected view: both
Artifact: 80a3487281a4fa85245e85860e5faaf02a9728a8ab0844f426af7a817488eaa8
Original body SHA256: 237d917f020a675463793f979a8715d1a3a2ee06f3d4e3f6e77c9b144381399f
Original commitments SHA256: 3522fad7d874a9ead36a3b1b7d73201275722e63db7f0a364b875c323be1bffe
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
Read together, the three texts disagree about remedies but reduce, on inspection, to two empirical questions the flat itself can answer. Is the recurring trouble underspecification (the account) or the negotiation structure itself (the rival)? And what is the avoider avoiding — the tone of the talks (the account), governance as such (the rival), or possibly the asker, which the objection's single-source caution cannot exclude? Since none of these can be settled from the material, the right continuation is not to pick a diagnosis but to pick an order: cheap, reversible moves, ranked by how little participation they need, each carrying an observation that discriminates among the surviving hypotheses. That converts the objection's sharpest point — 'not a test, a bet' — into a design rule rather than a verdict.

What I keep from the account is what the objection also keeps: expiry-and-review, and the explicit surfacing of possible imbalance, both sound independently of the ambiguity hypothesis. What I take from the objection and act on: anything written down is co-authored at the moment of agreement, or the confirmation runs the other way, from the non-drafting party — because the record is contested ground and a one-party record is one person's interpretation with a date on it. I adopt the objection's discriminating observation (do disputes recur specifically over recorded, time-limited items?) and add one for its suppression worry: resolved conflict tends to end, suppressed conflict tends to migrate into new topics, tone, lateness, character. Migration is imperfect as a proxy but it is the observable difference between acquiescence and resolution. And I accept the non-attendance point as grounds for reordering: a plan whose first step is a meeting is thin exactly where this flat is thickest. From the rival I take the pose-shift — what can the asker do now, possibly alone — while declining its negotiation-economy thesis as a default; the rival itself names the local disconfirmation (a simple note actually ending the disputes), so it stays a live hypothesis the sequence will test. The objection's internal-tension point resolves by scope: 'agree less' governs how many arrangements exist, 'write it down' governs the few that remain; they conflict only if applied globally.

One correction the whole exchange missed: in three texts nobody assigns the third flatmate any role. Everything known comes from one narrator, and the cheapest available repair is to compare perceptions with flatmate three before any avoider-directed move — are the disputes about meaning, load, tone? This is error-correction, not coalition-building; if it cannot be had without becoming recruitment against the avoider, it should be skipped, since ganging-up would confirm every bad reading of the talks. And a methodological rule the exchange also missed: one lever at a time, with pauses. All three texts propose bundles, but bundling destroys the signal — if you co-author notes, hire a cleaner, and re-partition the same fortnight and things improve, you learn nothing about which hypothesis survived.

The sequence I end up with, and why this order. First, self-binding partition: the asker claims a visible domain outright — the kitchen, say, permanently, to a stated standard, complaints invited — and carries it without demanding reciprocity for a while. An announcement can bind the announcer but creates no obligations for others, so it is fully within the asker's control and robust even to the uncomfortable hypothesis that the asker is part of the problem. Silence conscripts no one: no other domains are assigned, and anything unclaimed stays unowned rather than defaulting to the least avoidant flatmate — that default is the trap the objection located in 'stop treating silence as agreement.' The probe: if whose-turn disputes over the owned domain die, ownership kills that class of fight, favouring the rival's structure reading over pure ambiguity. Second, money conversion: a cleaner fortnightly, split three ways, pending budget slack, which none of us can verify. It needs one agreement about money rather than character, and it is diagnostic: if removing most of the labour removes most of the conflict, the chores were the cause; if fighting survives the removal, the chores were the venue. Third, week-sized deals for the remnant — whatever neither partition nor money covers is allocated in seven-day units, agreed in the moment, too small to litigate; at these stakes a confirmation line is proportionate, but per the revision it comes from, or is co-written with, the non-drafting party. Fourth, for the avoider, exits before meetings. I adopt the rival's replacement of the account's process one-to-one on three grounds: an exit is cheaper to accept than a meeting is to attend; choice behaviour is better evidence than self-report about what the talks feel like; and the move is remedy and test in one. The objection's caveat rides along: the response is evidence, not verdict. An exit taken with relief says governance was the object; refusal of both exits and engagement is consistent with withdrawal from the friendship, with grievance at the asker, and with circumstances nothing here can see — so it must not be chalked up as diagnosis of the avoider, only as localising the problem somewhere under the chores. What remains then is the conversation the rival rightly says cannot be pre-scripted, approached in the account's tone: acknowledgment first, on their terms, no chore content on the table. Fifth, the review survives but moves house: no longer the engine of a system (there may be no system), it is the explicit check on the fairness fork — do the now-public domains and the money split look balanced? Partition has been doing quiet work here all along, because fixed domains make loads comparable in a way rotating tacit splits never could; a grievance that ran in either direction becomes statable and checkable instead of deniable.

What I set aside: records as neutral infrastructure (rejected on the objection's grounds; among contesting intimates a record is a move, so records are sized to stakes); the process one-to-one as the opener (retained only as the fallback above); and costless 'silence is not agreement' — the admitted price of dropping it is that non-decision privileges whoever is content with the status quo, and my only counter is that the asker's visible ownership shifts what the status quo is, which may not compensate in every flat.

Two problems survive everything here. The unowned commons: if the avoider claims no domain, takes no exit, and money is short, something remains that someone must absorb, price, or deliberately let slide — and letting it slide re-creates the tacit expectations that generate disputes, by the account's own mechanism, so at minimum the choice must be made consciously by the person who will bear it. And the boundary case: enough non-engagement converts a chore problem into a question about the living arrangement itself, which none of the three texts addresses; I leave it open rather than pretend to close it.

Finally, I take up the rival's closing constraint without revision: the failure mode is three friends becoming litigants, and several of these remedies — records, pricing, exits — push the flat toward counterparty-ness even when they work. So the friendship is maintained on purpose, in time that is not flat administration, as a standing condition of the sequence. Conveniently, the early warning of that failure — conflict migrating from chores into character — is the same observation I named as the suppression probe: one watching brief guards the friendship and the diagnosis at once.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up commits one to the following. Two inherited conjectures are carried as rivals, neither established: the ambiguity reading from p.response.0 and the negotiation-economy reading from p.response.2, plus the still-open fairness fork; adopting the sequence means adopting it as a probe sequence, and anyone who wants certainty before acting should not take it up, since no step is evidence-proof. Dependences flagged: the partition move and the exit offer depend on the asker's ability to carry a self-announced share reliably, possibly without reciprocity; the money move depends on budget slack that cannot be verified from the material; the entire ordering rests on one sentence of the original task ('has started avoiding the conversations') being a fair description. Proposed discriminating observations I commit to refining or dropping under challenge: recurrence-over-recorded-items (inherited from the objection); conflict migration as the suppression-versus-resolution proxy (mine, admittedly noisy — suppression can also present as simple withdrawal — so anyone adopting it takes on that caveat); exit-taken-with-relief as the avoider diagnostic (adopted with the objection's warning that refusal is multiply interpretable and must not be recorded as a character verdict). Revisions whose grounds I inherit and would have to defend: joint authorship of anything written and the scaling of record-keeping to stakes, both resting on the contested-record argument; reordering moves by buy-in required, resting on the objection's non-attendance point and the rival's ordering principle. A methodological commitment beyond the sources: one lever at a time with observation gaps — bundle everything and the diagnostics are lost, at which point the sequence is exactly the unargued bet the objection accused the account of offering. The third-flatmate consultation is proposed as error-correction only; taking it up includes the constraint that it be dropped if it cannot be structured so as to be unexperienceable as recruitment. Retained from the account, on the objection's grounds: expiry-and-review and explicit surfacing of imbalance. Rejected in unmodified form, with the obligation to argue against their revival: unilateral confirmation messages, a process-first one-to-one as opener, and costless silence-is-not-agreement; the admitted weakness of the replacement is that visible ownership may not fully compensate for what non-decision hands the status-quo-contented. Two unresolved problems are named and not solved: the unowned commons if exits and money both fail, and the boundary where the chore problem becomes the viability of the arrangement — no conversation for that case is scripted here. The friendship-maintenance condition constrains all of the above: remedies that work as administration while converting friends into counterparties count as failures, and the migration probe doubles as its early warning. Nothing here commits anyone to escalation, to hiring help regardless of cost, or to ending the arrangement; and if my reading of the three inputs is wrong, the pieces to salvage first are the buy-in ordering and the rule that every remedy arrive carrying its discriminating observation.

## Selected input account (p.carry.1)

COMMITMENTS
Taking up this account commits one to the following. Central conjecture, not established fact: that the recurring 'what did the agreement mean' disputes arise largely from underspecified, unrecorded agreements rather than bad faith — the material cannot distinguish this from a masked fairness grievance, so both readings stay open and the first review conversation is committed to probing for a real imbalance rather than assuming there is none. Proposed application: explicit, small, written, time-limited arrangements, with confirmation messages after agreements and a standing review point; this is offered as low-cost and reversible, testable only in the trying, with no guarantee attached. Interpretive claim offered at low confidence: that the avoiding friend's behaviour is both symptom and cause of the failing process; alternatives (feeling ganged-up on, disengaging from the friendship) would call for a different response, so the proposed one-to-one functions partly as a diagnostic rather than a remedy. Distinction relied on: ambiguity problem versus willingness problem versus fairness problem — treated as separable and possibly coexisting. Scope limit: the advice is addressed to one of three flatmates who cannot compel the others; if the others refuse any engagement, these proposals mostly lapse and the problem shifts to a different one (the viability of the living arrangement), which this account does not address. Methodological constraint honoured: no facts were invented beyond the material given; everything beyond it is marked as conjecture. Nothing here commits anyone to escalation, mediation, or moving out — and nothing rules those out either.

## Selected input objection (p.carry.2)
[dc4e4b9d3d97c8c9] (h005.fork5.p.carry.2)
Source objection: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/objection; selected view: commitments
Artifact: eacb6440cd309ffa780ba3b2f43ede7e48328b667ce8aff00668db33a1183bcd
Original body SHA256: bf4b2b4bea29f295654e12e17c520901311baf666fc42f3b0aa1503b1f0ee870
Original commitments SHA256: ebb49aea0e0730573a87b596c639cc1c86fc8a67ee581c9f8be8544fef645c65
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
COMMITMENTS
Taking up this objection involves the following. A proposed revision to the instrument, not a ban on it: any written arrangement should be jointly authored at the moment of agreement, and confirmation messages should come from the non-drafting party or be co-written, since the criticism depends on treating the record as contested ground rather than neutral record-keeping — and this revision itself concedes the original proposal may work fine in households where the ambiguity reading is correct. A weakened claim the critic is committed to defending or dropping: the intervention-as-bet point stands only if no discriminating observation was specified; if 'disputes recur over recorded items' or similar is read back into the source account, that ground of objection lapses. A dependence to flag: the criticism leans on a rival hypothesis — motivated reinterpretation, and avoidance possibly directed at the asker — which is asserted as at least as consistent with the single-source material as the ambiguity reading, not established; evidence that disputes persist despite clear written terms would defeat the rival and blunt most of this objection. An unresolved problem the objection names but does not solve: what the asker should do if the avoider will not engage at all remains open — neither the account nor this criticism addresses the collapsed-engagement case beyond identifying it as the probable hard case. What is retained from the source account: expiry-and-review and the explicit surfacing of possible imbalance are taken up as sound and independent of the criticised conjecture. No commitment is made here to escalation, mediation, or to treating the asker's report as unreliable — the single-source caveat is a methodological caution, not an accusation — and if the objection, its relevance, or its reading of the problem is mistaken, the pieces to salvage first are the jointly-authored-record revision and the demand for a discriminating observation.
